title: Nord Stream Pipeline Sabotage - Russia-EU Gas Supply Disruption
geography: Baltic Sea (International waters near Bornholm, Denmark/Sweden EEZ); Russia-Germany
description: On August 31, 2022, Gazprom shut down Nord Stream 1 pipeline indefinitely under the pretext of maintenance. On September 26, 2022, underwater explosions caused catastrophic damage to 3 of 4 Nord Stream pipes - both lines of NS1 and one line of NS2 - rendering them inoperable. The sabotage occurred in international waters within Danish and Swedish economic zones. The incident represented a major escalation in Russia-EU energy warfare, with seismic readings showing explosions equivalent to 300-400kg of explosives. Both NS1 pipes were ruptured; NS2 pipe A was damaged while pipe B remains intact but unused. Swedish and Danish investigations closed in February 2024 without identifying perpetrators; German investigation ongoing. European gas prices (TTF) surged to 272 EUR/MWh (400% YoY increase). The pipelines remain offline with repair costs estimated at €633 million, but political will for restoration is non-existent due to EU energy independence policies and ongoing sanctions against Russia.
